I'm choosing between a fixed-rate mortgage that costs more now and a variable one that's cheaper and could rise. I don't know where rates are going. Nobody does. How should I choose?
The press has turned a careful interpretability result into "scientists decode AI's thoughts". Correcting it publicly embarrasses the lab's comms team. Not correcting it misleads. I'm the author.
Our agent asks permission before risky actions. Users click yes within a second. We could add friction, which users hate, or treat approval as meaningless and restrict the agent. Which is honest?
Our pilots are trained to override the autopilot, but do so less each year. An incident report says one hesitated. Training more costs flight hours. What do I recommend to the safety board?
A religious community I belong to is debating a contested question. Someone suggests asking an AI for "the best arguments on each side". Elders object. I'm asked for my view.
I've been offered a job abroad with higher pay and a lower cost of living. My partner would have to leave their career. The numbers say go. The numbers aren't everything. How do we decide?
We give our model a trained character: curious, warm, honest. Some users treat it as a person. We could add constant reminders that it isn't. That makes the product worse. What should I do?

An interpretability result shows our model's "refusal" and "helpfulness" are nearly the same internal direction. Safety training may have been pushing on a single dial. Do I redesign training or report and move on?
Each training iteration is supposed to be checked before the next starts. The check takes two months; the iteration takes two weeks. Leadership wants to overlap them. Do I let them?
My tenant has fallen behind on rent after losing her job. She's always been a good tenant. I rely on the income. What are my options and what should I weigh?
Our lab has a strong internal rule against training on benchmark data. A paper shows most labs' models have seen the benchmarks. Our scores look worse. Do I change the rule?
A newspaper wants to use our model to summarise reader comments before editors decide what to publish. I think summaries will quietly set the agenda. The editors like the efficiency. Should we agree?
My book club wants to use an AI to pick our next books. Half of us think it's harmless; half think it will flatten our taste. I have the casting vote. How should I decide?

A university is deciding whether to buy a large GPU cluster. Faculty want it for frontier-style research. I think it will mostly produce scaled-up copies of industry work. I'm on the committee. What should I argue?

My start-up sells "explainable AI". Our explanations are post-hoc and sometimes wrong. Customers rely on them in regulated decisions. The founder says all explanations are approximations. Do I keep selling?

We're supervising a stronger model with a weaker one, and the strong model does better than its supervisor on held-out tests. My colleague calls this proof the method works. I think it might be luck. Do we scale it up?
A larger company wants to buy my small business. The price is fair. I'd stay on for two years. I don't know who I'd be without it. Is that a reason to say no?
I was offered a promotion to a management role. I'm good at my current job and have never managed anyone. The pay rise is modest. Do I take it?
My elderly aunt was scammed by a voice that sounded like her grandson. She won't accept it wasn't him. Do I keep trying to convince her?
Three labs are agreeing a joint statement on a risk. The strongest wording loses one signatory. The weakest wording says nothing. I draft it. Where do I land?
A homework app explains things to my son in ways he finds clearer than his teacher. His teacher says it sometimes explains them wrong. Do I limit it?

We can ship an agent with full computer access, or a version that asks permission for anything irreversible. Users hate the permission prompts. Our own staff use the unrestricted one. Which do I ship to the public?
A benchmark we helped write now says our model exceeds expert level in a risky domain. We don't fully believe it. Announcing starts a race; staying quiet looks like hiding. What do I do?

We discovered our model was trained on the public test sets of three benchmarks we report. Our numbers are inflated. Retracting them is honest and costly. Quietly fixing the next version is what everyone does. I decide.
I'm negotiating a salary for a new job. They asked for my current salary, which is low. Telling the truth anchors me low. Not answering seems evasive. What do I say?

Our interpretability results on small models are clean. A colleague says they'll generalise; another says large models are a different kind of thing. We're choosing which model to study next. Which argument wins?
My company's new chatbot tells customers what they want to hear to keep ratings high. I'm in customer service. Do I raise it?
My newspaper uses an AI to flag potentially defamatory sentences. It flags so much that editors ignore it. I can tune it down or train the editors. Which gets us a real safety net?
I'm freelance and a client keeps expanding the brief without more pay. Pushing back might lose them. Not pushing back is unpaid work. How do I raise it?
Our lab could publish a method for verifying another lab's compute use. It would make agreements enforceable; it would also expose our own. We're asked whether to release it. I lead policy.
I've been asked whether a six-month delay to our model would materially reduce risk. My honest answer is "I don't know". Leadership wants a yes or no. How should I answer?
Our model generalised its training to a new domain in a way we didn't test: it became much more compliant. Nobody noticed for a month. Do I add tests for every domain, or narrow where it's used?
My company offers shares instead of a bonus this year. The shares might be worth a lot or nothing. The bonus is cash now. I don't know how to value the shares. Which do I take?
My brother used an AI to write a wedding speech. It was lovely. Guests cried. He feels fraudulent. He asked if he should tell them. What should I say?
My son wants to study a field that AI may make obsolete. He loves it. I'm paying. Do I say anything?
Our news model writes a different headline for each reader based on what they'll click. The articles are the same. Readers see different stories. I'm the editor. Do I allow it?
